context.objective: Document how we carry out LOC Draw & Repayment Execution, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The document asks the team to classify the trigger as contractual, lender-driven, or client-planned, but doesn’t describe how it reaches them. How does the trigger usually come to your attention?

It reaches my team, the fund and capital-activity team, as a communication from the client or from the lender. In practice the work starts when there is a draw request, when an investment or management fees are expected to be funded from the line of credit, when a repayment is due, or when the client plans to repay from proceeds. There is no fixed schedule, it happens whenever one of those events comes up. If the request comes in verbally or it is incomplete, we get written confirmation from the client before we do anything else, because a conversation on its own does not authorize the action.
Once written confirmation is in, what does your team do first?

The first thing is what is in the document I uploaded. We work out what kind of event it is, so a draw, a repayment, anticipated investment funding, or repayment of fees that were previously funded by the line of credit. Then we confirm the legal facility, the borrowing entity, the purpose, the requested date, and the required amount and date if those are known, and we record whether the trigger is contractual, lender-driven or client-planned. All of that goes into the event and facility record, and what we come out with is a validated event request. The check at that point is that the correct facility, entity and purpose are confirmed before any calculation starts. The document only covers the opening of the work, up to deciding the funding path, so I can talk you through the rest from there.
How do you determine the funding path for a repayment, including whether available cash is sufficient?

We do that together with the client. We take the liquidity position from the working-capital report and the bank records and hold it against the proposed repayment amount to see whether available cash covers it. The decision has to be based on reconciled cash and the forward obligations we already know about. If cash is not enough, the options are to call capital, use approved distribution proceeds, defer if the facility terms permit that, or escalate, and it is the client who decides. We document the client's timing and amount decisions, and the result is an approved funding path kept in the capital-activity file. If cash turns out to be insufficient or it changes later, the working-capital review is done again and the client decides again. I don't know who the internal owner of the insufficient-cash decision is on our side, that has not been set, so the process owner would have to confirm it.
For a draw, how do you confirm the available borrowing capacity and that no listed issue blocks it?

That part is not done by my team. The facility compliance preparer and reviewer give us the current capacity and compliance status, and they work from the compliance certificate and the facility tracker. The borrowing-base calculation and the facility certification themselves belong to that separate facility compliance process, we only take the result, and it has to be current as of the proposed draw. What has to be true before a draw is that there is current supported capacity and no blocking term. If capacity is not available or there is a breach, we stop, the draw request is not submitted, and the issue is resolved through the facility compliance process. Depending on the issue it is the client, the Director or the lender who decides, and nothing proceeds until it is resolved and documented. The record we keep is the capacity and compliance check. Whether there is a separate approver for that check beyond the compliance preparer and reviewer has not been specified, so I can't tell you that, the process owner would need to confirm it.
Once current capacity and compliance are clear, how does your team confirm the draw’s approved purpose and planned use, and what happens next?

For a draw we confirm the purpose and the planned use of the funds with the client, from the client's written approved instruction, and it has to fit the permitted purpose in the latest executed facility agreement and its amendments. What happens next depends on the kind of event. For a repayment, the fund and capital-activity preparer calculates the amount in the capital-activity Excel model. They compare the principal with the lender statement and the facility tracker, confirm whether interest is paid in cash or capitalized, pull actual interest through the last approved date, which is commonly quarter-end, project interest from that date to the planned event date, document the rates, day-count assumptions, dates and calculation basis, and then add principal, accrued interest and projected interest together. Actual and estimated amounts have to be kept separate. For a draw, the next thing is the draw request. The lender's loan request form is completed with the amount, the purpose and the applicable repayment terms, matched to the capacity and compliance records, signed internally and by the client, and submitted to the lender through the approved channel, and we keep the submission record. The amount must not exceed the approved capacity. I don't know who is supposed to prepare and submit that form, who the signatories are, or what the submission cutoff time is. None of that is confirmed and the process owner would need to say.
Once the repayment amount is calculated, what happens next to arrange and complete the repayment?

First it goes into capital activity. My team enters the repayment and the interest in the capital-event inputs when capital has to be called, and we include the amount in the cash modeling before, during and after the event. If the repayment depends on distribution proceeds we line up the timing, but we never treat projected proceeds as cash already received. Then comes the client review. We present the principal, the interest basis, the estimate period, the funding path and the timing, record the client's comments and update the model, and if the event date changes we refresh the projected interest and it is reviewed again. Once the client approves we mark the instruction as final, and the client has to have approved the final amount and date before anything is executed. After that the fund team or the GL preparer initiates or posts the GL entry, and then Treasury completes the payment checks, which include an independent phone callback verification and the approvals, and executes the cash movement with the lender or bank. If the GL posting is not approved and complete, cash is not released. I can't tell you the exact accounts or the journal entry, that is not specified, and I also don't know what form the client approval takes or who the approving authority is. Once the cash has moved we reconcile and close the event.
What does your team compare after the cash moves to reconcile and close the event?

The fund team does that together with Treasury. We compare the amount that was actually executed with the approved request or repayment instruction, and the lender or bank record, the facility tracker, the GL and the cash view all have to agree. Then we update the principal, the accrued interest, the maturity and duration dates and the facility tracker, and we update the categorized cash in the working-capital view. If anything was rejected, only partly applied or misapplied, we resolve it, and if the execution differs from what was approved, Treasury and the fund team investigate, correct it and escalate. The event cannot be closed until the cash, the lender record, the GL and the approved amount agree. Last, we file the facility documents, the model, the approval, the GL record, the bank record and the reconciliation in the digital binder. Two things I don't know are what tolerance is allowed on the reconciliation and who formally reviews and signs off that the event is complete. Neither has been specified.
What can happen if a draw or repayment is delayed or executed incorrectly?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

For repayment, the event is reconciled and closed after cash has moved.
The steps from draw-request submission to cash movement remain unclear.

The internal owner of the insufficient-cash decision has not been set; the process owner would need to confirm it.

For repayment, the documented funding-path step determines whether cash is sufficient and whether a capital call is required or distribution proceeds will be used. For a draw, it confirms approved purpose and planned use; client timing and amount decisions are documented.
If a request is verbal or incomplete, the fund and capital-activity team obtains written client confirmation before doing anything else.

For repayment, the team works with the client to compare liquidity from the working-capital report and bank records with the proposed repayment, considering reconciled cash and known forward obligations.
If cash is insufficient, the client decides among calling capital, using approved distribution proceeds, deferring if facility terms permit, or escalating. If cash is insufficient or changes later, the working-capital review is repeated and the client decides again.
The team documents the client's timing and amount decisions; the resulting approved funding path is kept in the capital-activity file.
For a draw, the facility compliance preparer and reviewer provide current capacity and compliance status using the compliance certificate and facility tracker. The result must be current as of the proposed draw.
If capacity is unavailable or there is a breach, the team stops and does not submit the draw request. The issue is resolved through facility compliance; depending on the issue, the client, Director or lender decides, and nothing proceeds until resolution is documented.
For a draw, the team confirms purpose and planned use with the client using the client's written approved instruction, against the permitted purpose in the latest executed facility agreement and amendments.
For repayment, the fund and capital-activity preparer calculates the amount in the capital-activity Excel model: compare principal to the lender statement and facility tracker, confirm cash payment or capitalization of interest, pull actual interest through the last approved date, commonly quarter-end, and project interest to the planned event date. The preparer documents rates, day-count assumptions, dates and basis, then adds principal, accrued interest and projected interest, keeping actual and estimated amounts separate.
For a draw, the lender's loan request form is completed with amount, purpose and applicable repayment terms, matched to capacity and compliance records, signed internally and by the client, and submitted to the lender through the approved channel. The submission record is retained.
The participant does not know who prepares and submits the draw form, who signs it, or the submission cutoff; the process owner needs to confirm these.
When capital must be called for repayment, the fund and capital-activity team enters repayment and interest in capital-event inputs and includes the amount in cash modeling before, during and after the event. If repayment depends on distribution proceeds, the team aligns timing without treating projected proceeds as received cash.
The team presents the client with principal, interest basis, estimate period, funding path and timing, records comments and updates the model. If the event date changes, projected interest is refreshed and reviewed again. After client approval, the instruction is marked final.
After client approval, the fund team or GL preparer initiates or posts the GL entry. Treasury then completes payment checks, including an independent phone callback and approvals, and executes cash movement with the lender or bank. The event is reconciled and closed after cash moves.
The participant does not know the exact accounts or journal entry for the GL posting.
After cash moves, the fund team and Treasury compare the executed amount with the approved request or repayment instruction and ensure the lender or bank record, facility tracker, GL and cash view agree.
The team updates principal, accrued interest, maturity and duration dates and the facility tracker, and updates categorized cash in the working-capital view. Rejected, partly applied or misapplied items are resolved; Treasury and the fund team investigate, correct and escalate differences from the approved execution.

The document calls for confirmation that no covenant, LPA, maturity, duration, concentration or certification issue blocks the event, and identification of required lender and client forms and approvals. It does not assign the checks or approvals to roles.
For a verbal or incomplete request, the team obtains written client confirmation before proceeding.

The participant cannot identify the internal or client signatories on the draw request; the process owner must confirm them.
The client reviews principal, interest basis, estimate period, funding path and timing; comments are recorded and the model updated. A changed event date causes projected interest to be refreshed and reviewed again. Client approval of the final amount and date is required before execution.

The document distinguishes draw and repayment paths: draw capacity and purpose are confirmed, while repayment funding is assessed against cash, a capital call or distribution proceeds.
A verbal or incomplete request adds an initial written-client-confirmation step before the team proceeds.
When repayment cash is insufficient or changes later, the working-capital review and client decision are repeated; insufficient cash also introduces alternative funding, deferral or escalation options.

The repayment assessment uses liquidity information from the working-capital report; the working-capital review is repeated if cash is insufficient or changes later.

The participant specifically describes current capacity and compliance work for draws. steps.title: Receive LOC event communication
steps.description: A communication from the client or lender brings a draw request, expected investment or management-fee funding, a repayment due, or planned repayment from proceeds to the team. Events arise as needed.

steps.title: Is the request verbal or incomplete?
steps.description: Identify whether the request is verbal or incomplete. In either case written client confirmation is required before other work; a conversation alone does not authorize action.

steps.title: Obtain written client confirmation
steps.description: For a verbal or incomplete request, obtain written client confirmation before doing anything else. Handling of delayed or absent confirmation is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm event and facility
steps.system: Event and facility record; underlying system UNKNOWN
steps.description: Identify a draw, repayment, anticipated investment funding, or repayment of fees previously funded by the LOC. Confirm the legal facility, borrowing entity, purpose, requested date, and required amount and date if known. Record the details and whether the trigger is contractual, lender-driven or client-planned. Confirm the correct facility, entity and purpose before calculation. The supplied procedure also directs these opening actions.

steps.title: Is draw capacity and compliance clear?
steps.actor: Facility compliance preparer and reviewer provide status; fund and capital-activity team receives it
steps.description: For a draw, obtain current capacity and compliance status from the separate facility compliance process and keep the capacity and compliance check. Capacity must be supported and current as of the proposed draw, with no blocking term. Borrowing-base calculation and facility certification are performed in facility compliance, not by the participant's team.

steps.title: Stop and resolve blocked draw
steps.actor: Resolution performers UNKNOWN; client, Director or lender decides depending on issue
steps.description: Do not submit the draw if capacity is unavailable or there is a breach. Resolve the issue through the separate facility compliance process. Depending on the issue, the client, Director or lender decides; nothing proceeds until resolution is documented. The resumption point is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm draw purpose and use
steps.actor: Fund and capital-activity team with client
steps.description: Confirm the draw purpose and planned use with the client from its written approved instruction. They must fit the permitted purpose in the latest executed facility agreement and amendments. Handling a mismatch is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Complete lender draw request
steps.description: Complete the form with amount, purpose and applicable repayment terms; match it to capacity and compliance records. The amount must not exceed approved capacity. The preparer is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Sign and submit draw request
steps.actor: Internal and client signatories; submitter UNKNOWN
steps.system: Approved lender channel; specific channel UNKNOWN
steps.description: Have the form signed internally and by the client, submit it to the lender through the approved channel and keep the submission record. Signatory identities, signature order, submitter and cutoff are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is repayment cash sufficient?
steps.actor: Fund and capital-activity team with client
steps.description: Compare liquidity from the working-capital report and bank records with the proposed repayment. Base the decision on reconciled cash and known forward obligations. If cash is insufficient, the client chooses a path.

steps.title: Which funding path does the client choose?
steps.description: If cash is insufficient, the client decides whether to call capital, use approved distribution proceeds, defer if facility terms permit, or escalate. Following a repeated working-capital review, the client decides again. The internal GPFS owner of the insufficient-cash decision has not been set. Option-specific downstream routes for deferral and escalation are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Document approved funding path
steps.description: Document the client's timing and amount decisions and keep the approved funding path in the capital-activity file. How a sufficient-cash decision reaches this record and the exact relationship to repayment calculation are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Repeat working-capital review
steps.description: If cash turns out to be insufficient or changes later, repeat the working-capital review and have the client decide again. The later cash-change entry point and review performer are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate repayment amount
steps.system: Capital-activity Excel model; lender statement; facility tracker
steps.description: Compare principal with the lender statement and facility tracker and confirm whether interest is paid in cash or capitalized. Pull actual interest through the last approved date, commonly quarter-end, and project interest to the planned event date. Document rates, day-count assumptions, dates and calculation basis; add principal, accrued interest and projected interest. Keep actual and estimated amounts separate.

steps.title: Include repayment in capital activity
steps.description: When capital must be called, enter the repayment and interest in capital-event inputs. Include the amount in cash modeling before, during and after the event.

steps.title: Align distribution proceeds timing
steps.description: If repayment depends on distribution proceeds, align the timing. Do not treat projected proceeds as cash already received.

steps.title: Review repayment with client
steps.actor: Fund and capital-activity team and client
steps.description: Present principal, interest basis, estimate period, funding path and timing to the client. Record comments and update the model. If the event date changes, refresh projected interest and have it reviewed again.

steps.title: Refresh projected interest
steps.description: When the event date changes, refresh projected interest and have it reviewed again.

steps.title: Finalize approved instruction
steps.actor: Client and fund and capital-activity team
steps.description: Once the client approves, mark the instruction final. The client must approve the final amount and date before execution. Approval format and approving authority are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Initiate or post GL entry
steps.description: After the instruction is finalized, initiate or post the GL entry. Cash cannot be released unless the GL posting is approved and complete. Exact accounts, journal and GL approval responsibility are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Complete Treasury payment checks
steps.description: Complete payment checks, including independent phone callback verification and approvals. Approval authorities, retained evidence and failure handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Execute repayment cash movement
steps.system: Channel UNKNOWN; lender or bank is the counterparty
steps.description: Execute the cash movement with the lender or bank after payment checks and approvals. Do not release cash unless the GL posting is approved and complete.

steps.title: Compare execution and records
steps.system: Lender or bank record, facility tracker, GL and cash view
steps.description: Compare the executed amount with the approved request or repayment instruction. The lender or bank record, facility tracker, GL and cash view must agree. Identify rejected, partly applied or misapplied items and execution differences.

steps.title: Update facility and cash records
steps.description: Update principal, accrued interest, maturity and duration dates and the facility tracker; update categorized cash in the working-capital view.

steps.title: Resolve application exceptions
steps.description: Resolve any rejected, partly applied or misapplied item. Resolution method, evidence and return point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Investigate execution differences
steps.description: If execution differs from what was approved, investigate, correct and escalate. The escalation recipient and subsequent handoff are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Close reconciled event
steps.actor: Fund team and Treasury; formal sign-off role UNKNOWN
steps.description: Close the event after reconciliation. Closure is blocked until cash, the lender record, GL and approved amount agree. The allowed tolerance and formal reviewer or sign-off role are unspecified.

steps.title: File event records
steps.actor: Fund team and Treasury; individual filer UNKNOWN
steps.description: File the facility documents, model, approval, GL record, bank record and reconciliation in the digital binder.

steps.title: Check documented event requirements
steps.description: Document-only opening step: the procedure directs confirmation that no covenant, LPA, maturity, duration, concentration or certification issue blocks the event, and identification of required lender and client forms and approvals. It also directs confirmation of borrowing capacity for a draw. The participant describes a capacity and compliance check for draws, but current practice and responsibility for these documented actions on repayment events are UNKNOWN.
